Finally, to destroy the record that the Dharma Sangham was established, two almirahs were lifted from Sivagiri, brought to a rock at the place where the watcher Kunhiraman lived on the southern side of the Sivagiri school, and burnt. Is it the monk order that won by presenting a copy signed by the Swami stating "I have resigned from the SNDP in thought, word, and deed" at Sankarasubbayyar's bench, that is showing all this today? Shouldn't we remember the incident where Ayurvedic acharya Bhargavan Vaidyar was beaten and his keys were snatched away, alleging that he took the side of the monks back then? He was someone who was adopted, raised, and taught Ayurveda by the Swami.

There is clear evidence as to how you view Narayana Guru. Worldly householders might lack that knowledge. It brings sorrow that the monks have lost it. The act of praising the ideal to the skies and installing the Shivalinga in the heart is something even a worldly devotee cannot conceive. Narayana Guru did not think of installing this Shivalinga inside. It was to increase the greatness of sacrifice and lead human life to salvation. This has become an action plan that ties one down even below ordinary people, rather than that of an ascetic. This is not suitable for a ritualist, a devotee, a wise man, or even a modern devotee. Who with a perfect mind wouldn't think that devotion, if it degrades, shouldn't stoop this low!

Vairavan Shanthi, a man from Vakkom, became Shanthi Swami and attained Samadhi at Aruvippuram after living up to the age of one hundred and fourteen. You must have known about that ascetic. Once Narayana Guru lay down to sleep, he would lie across the door of that room. When the Swami got up at night without him knowing and crossed over, a man as tall as Kuttichathan would go with him. One day, upon reaching near the neem tree on the northern side of the temple—I don't know if that neem tree is still there today—a globe of light was conversing with the Swami. The Swami was enveloped in light. Seeing this, the Shanthi fell to the ground trembling with fear, and the Swami lifted him up, gave him water, and asked, "Do you have to come with me everywhere?" If you remembered at least this incident, you wouldn't have been able to show such a heart-linga. It would have been enough if you had at least respected what was written about Chidambaram.
Brahmamukhamaravandithalingam
Janmajaramarananthakalingam
Karmanivaranakaushalalingam
Thanmridu pathu chidambaralingam
The Swami, who started writing thus, wrote so for the worldly devotees, and the final verse of the Atmopadesa Satakam—
Athumithumalla sadarthamallaham sa-
cchidamruthamennu thelinju dheeranayi
sadasadithi prathipathiyattu satho-
mithai mruduvay mruduvayamarnnidenam ٹ
If you had only thought about the meaning of that 'mridu' (soft) and the meaning of 'Sat Om', you wouldn't have drawn this farce.

If I explain further, it might hurt some people. I doubt they will like it. I happily accept such Sri Narayana devotees proclaiming that I am against Sri Narayana. But I am sure that I will not face the heartbroken opposition of that ascetic. Your jubilation seems to once again pour sorrow into life. Can there be a greater ignorance shown towards Narayana Guru than this? If you only advertised that it was people among them who brought a stay order to prevent the Swami's fortieth-day bathing ceremony, all the people today would have seen the Swami as venerable. I am completely confident that there would have been no need for the fate we see today—calling the community members, building platforms, and making them clap for meaningless political speeches as Sukumar Azhikode reminded us.

Likewise, I am convinced that none of those who were in Sivagiri in 1130 [Malayalam Era] can say that I am against Sivagiri. The fools who say many such things and try to bring ruin not just to Narayana Guru's legacy but to the world itself can only be described as contemporaries of the earth-shaking bird. It will be enough if you truthfully reveal at least some of the things I have said here—to understand that Narayana Guru did good for the world. Please forgive me. May you feel better sense at least tomorrow! May God forgive the flaws of the deeds you are doing today!
Guruvani
March 1988

We haven't been able to lead a life suited to the times. There is no need to perform the duties of the Treta Yuga in the Kali Yuga. Nor the duties of the Dvapara. Doesn't Kali have a dharma? If each yuga has its own dharma, isn't there a dharma that belongs to this Kali? If so, what should be done in this Kali? What is Kali dharma? This is a flaw. Another thing, the royal rule and the Vedic mutts of those times kept us far away, not even giving us the alphabet. With that, we became ignorant people without the dharma to perform duties with knowledge. So what will he do? 'The lord's rice and the slave's back' - because of living like this, we have never seen anything called freedom directly.

Thus, there is no education, no wealth, no lordship. No merit of having lived an orderly life. Then, instead of worshiping God, they caught hold of some forest or corner and danced (in trance). After that, in the temple system shown by the Vedic priests, in the Trimurti system, from the most degraded Bhadrakali temple to Madan, Marutha, Mantramoorthi, and Yantramoorthi, doing pooja out of mere chaos, isn't it a lifestyle tied down to this? How can you consider this as divine worship? Both of these are mistakes.

How should we change from this? Two other things have happened to you from these two mistakes. One, the merit of birth was lost. Or even if there is merit, it resulted in a tragedy where you didn't know how to keep it as your own. So you were destroyed that way too. If there is merit, a life that acts as a safeguard for the home, land, and country should be derived from him. Along with that, in the ignorance displayed by this statecraft, everyone was left without freedom. In this situation, you have lost that part.

Then, isn't it you who should know what to achieve it with? Countless great souls have told you about it. But you haven't taken it up. Buddha, Parayi Petta Panthirukulam, eighteen Siddhars - this is how they passed among us. But now only two groups have moved away from this Shudra class and come forward a little. Although they have come forward, their culture is very bad. One is the path of Moses and Jesus. The other is the path of the Prophet. They alone came into a monotheistic belief. After Islam, those who came into monotheism are few. Even though all this is said among Christians today, two sides have emerged: the depressed Christian and the good Christian. This too is an aspect of Indian culture. So, if this culture spreads everywhere, if we attain education, wealth, and lordship today, it will be as if we have attained some kind of greatness.

What are we doing today? How much bribe do you have to pay to educate a child from nursery and make them a doctor? How much bribe will you pay as an admission fee? Aren't you paying at least two lakh rupees now? To my knowledge, they pay two lakh ten thousand and then sing a song of recommendation. If it is taken as a bribe, it is like this. That too is not here, but in Madras or Bangalore. I mentioned this was taken in Bangalore—to become a doctor. For engineering, it is seventy-five thousand. Why are you so interested in paying such extortionate amounts? You have seen some other loot elsewhere, haven't you? Isn't it to reap a loot in return? Otherwise, someone might say that he is honest now. Except for that one person, there will be no one else. Thus, we have been taught a system of giving a loot to get a loot in return. How will you change from this? Where does this mentioned part stand in your good deeds?

Having believed in this for a while, when the program failed despite employing tantra, mantra, and yantra, some people said they do not believe in it. Some others called it useless, nonsense, and various other things. Still others claimed it was because these were not completed properly. Another group argued that this was a completely different method. Thinking in various ways like this, we became divided.
Guruvani
April 1988

A sannyasin achieves fruition through his diligence and sacrifice. This is something that not only Hindus but all human beings should know. When a person with such sacrifice, or someone belonging to a guru lineage, steps into a place, a house, or a compound, he feels that whatever needs to happen there, a scene involving his sacrifice should be created for them. Only a renunciate (thyagi) will feel that way. Others will not feel so. They will only try to extract something from wherever they go. In general, human understanding is like that. It is not so for a renunciate. He will not have any desire to earn something for himself or any desire other than the merit of his own soul. Having lived for a long time like this, taking many births, all these powers of penance will unite to attain supreme knowledge (jnana). It is after attaining this knowledge that one emerges as a Guru. When a wise person (jnani) is born, he is born knowing nothing about the path of wisdom. But once he grows up, he will have established a movement or something else.

From there, the work begins again. It is this work that has been pre-ordained by the Divine for the welfare of the world. Such a worker, or his guru lineage, wherever they go, whether they walk on the street or anywhere else, will constantly observe how the houses and the land are situated. As a thinker or a writer walks from one end to another, he will grasp the pattern of that place. What does a sannyasin do when he becomes a jnani? He does not look at the pattern. How was the ancient period here? What have the people adopted as its medium? What is the character of this land? What has happened to the country? What is going to happen in the future? He contemplates all this. Then, if anything can be done there, he will do it through his divine resolve (sankalpa). Such gurus come only once in a long while. Such great souls arrive only when the land faces destruction or when the whole world is on the verge of ruin. They will continuously work from one end to the other. They will act both through people and independently.

Five such gurus will come for a Chaturyuga (a cycle of four yugas). It is through such gurus that this world gains stability. If the nature of this work is not explained to the land, the home, and every individual, the welfare of the land will not endure. While they make a divine resolve, the actual action lies in the hands of the people in the world. The Guru will reform them in whatever way is necessary—by instilling a little fear, offering some love, using some willpower, and imparting some enthusiasm. What happens otherwise? The evil tendencies of the land will act and advance. That is why it is said that a country without virtuous people is ruined.

Good people (Sadhus) means righteous people. It is from them that we and the country receive blessedness. If the knowledgeable ones among the contemporaries are acting as part of a guru lineage, their desire will be a prayer to the Almighty to make them work in a way that brings everlasting peace and harmony to that land and its people. Others are not like that. They will be acting only to show off their grandeur. The operational capacity based on grandeur will not last. However, because of faith, something might happen. But it will not endure. Just like the renunciate, those standing closest to him will also continue to work.

When working, some people may incur certain faults. How this happens is that while they are working, either a word they dislike will be directed at them, or as they progress in their work, they might say something that hurts someone else. That word will have absolutely no connection to the knowledge they have spoken of until then. They might be speaking very profound words. It will seem as though they possess all the knowledge in this world. But in the very next moment, they might utter a word that hurts someone.

Every worker must realize that everyone has a character flaw. God has given us an opportunity to eradicate this. The firm resolve that 'I will not waste this opportunity' should be undertaken willingly, just like a sacrifice. Those who do not like it cannot do it. I will resolve this character flaw of mine and thereby earn spiritual merit. One should not become insignificant after resolving it. If performed with the sense of dedication that I should be made to perform an action which earns merit and resolves the evils afflicting my home, my land, and my country, it will be completely eradicated in three years. What remains is that we can work for that goodness. After working for goodness, its greatness will manifest after death. Even the maternal ancestors will be purified.
Guruvani
May 1988

It is hoped that the unexpected displacement at Sivagiri will serve as an occasion not only for Sivagiri but also for the believers of Narayana Guru and the lineage that loves the acharyas to accept it as a model, and for the members of the Dharma Sangham to attain complete strength. It is known that it is not right to judge the past leaders of the Dharma Sangham for anything other than a good purpose. However, it is painful that a Secretary worked for seventeen years as if he were everything for the Dharma Sangham on behalf of that SNDP, for which the Guru had to write that he resigns from the SNDP Yogam in thought, word, and deed. In other words, their actions only succeeded in creating an impression among other community members that the Dharma Sangham belongs not to Narayana Guru but to the SNDP, and that the Swami worked for the community.

I remember advocate P. Madhavan, who belonged to the same community, writing an article in Kerala Kaumudi when such speeches and actions were taking place, purportedly for the sake of the community. That article made it clear that Narayana Guru was not someone who thought about eradicating caste in a trivial manner. Similarly, although many people were deeply hurt, they were in a helpless situation where they could not speak out or act because they lacked the means to do so. The intelligent and capable people within the community caused considerable pain to the Swami while he was alive, in their attempt to make him the property of the SNDP. The ignorance of the community leaders of that time distressed the Swami at the felicitation meeting for his sixtieth birthday, held at the Alappuzha Kidangamparambu temple ground. The harassment that began that day continued until the time of his Samadhi. Even three days prior to his Samadhi, without giving him any peace, they troubled him by approaching him with a will to bequeath assets for the community. Having worked for this cause for eleven years, when the Swami realized that they would only stand contrary to his ideals, he was heartbroken and wrote, "I resign from the SNDP in thought, word, and deed." On his way to Madras for Dr. Pandala's treatment, he gathered others and registered the Dharma Sangham, consisting of fourteen members, at Koorkanchery in Thrissur. It was because Thrissur was under British rule at that time that the Swami accomplished this there itself. The present-day Dharma Sangham must be able to deeply comprehend this pain of the Guru and rectify the errors. It is for this purpose that all this is being documented at this juncture.

Nataraja Guru was also included among the fourteen members of the Dharma Sangham at that time. He was excluded from the Dharma Sangham only because he affixed one signature on the bylaw but refrained from putting the second signature. However, the members of the Dharma Sangham did not show any lack of affection towards Nataraja Guru. The evidence for this is that Nataraja Guru was selected as the advisor to the Dharma Sangham during the tenure of Swami Achyuthananda. When the Swami slapped a young man named G.N. Das, who served as Swami Achyuthananda's cook, for some mistake, he took him along, departed to the Gurukulam, and resigned from the position of advisor. After that incident, he did not behave affectionately towards Sivagiri. He would visit Sivagiri, pay his respects, and leave, but maintained no other relationship. On that occasion, Swami Brahmananda and I went to the Gurukulam. At that time, Swami Brahmananda was known as Narayanan. Having joined the army and returned during the time of Swami Achyuthananda, he had left in displeasure because he was not conferred the name Brahmanandan. It was when he returned to Sivagiri again and was working as a clerk there that the two of us visited the Gurukulam. While discussing various matters concerning Narayana Guru there, Nataraja Guru made a remark: "Yes, the Swami had to act in such a manner back then." Upon hearing this, we did not stay much longer; we had to leave after briefly discussing this very matter.

Within two months of saying this, he prepared to depart for America. I was performing pooja at the Samadhi at that time. Nataraja Guru arrived at the Samadhi accompanied by a saffron-clad individual who went by the name Paramanandan. He asked Nataraja Guru, "What should we expect regarding your ability to make Narayana Guru known to the outside world once you go to America?" The reply was, "If the circumstances are favorable, and if God provides the opportunity, I hope to be able to do what is necessary." A year and a half after his departure, a letter arrived for the Madathipathi Swami at Sivagiri, which read as follows: "I am reminded of the proverb that the jasmine in the front yard has no fragrance—because, sometime after arriving there, I was able to reside on top of a mountain, secured accommodation in a room next to the British Government Library, and was able to refer to British Philosophy. Thus, I was able to read clearly about Islam, Hinduism, the Parsis, the propagation of Christianity by the Portuguese, and their period of governance. I have also been able to evaluate Jesus." This is how the first letter proceeded. Two more letters arrived subsequently. Each letter would typically arrive after an interval of ten or fifteen months.

"It is only now that I have completely understood Narayana Guru. I feel distressed when I realize that I received a first-class merely for writing down two lines from Narayana Guru's *Darshanamala*." Nataraja Guru, who until then had not believed in touching the Guru's feet or in the Indian monastic traditions, wrote in his final letter, "When I return there, I will certainly proclaim the Guru's greatness and customs to the people." As a result of instructing Swami Sankarananda that all three of these letters should be read in the prayer meeting, they were indeed read aloud. The time of his return to Varkala from America and the specific train he would arrive on were also communicated.

The locals and Sivagiri jointly organized a reception at the railway station. That was a period when the Dharma Sangham was split into two factions, and the conflict was at its peak. A year prior to that—in the Malayalam year 1125—Swami Nijananda was standing ousted and excommunicated. He approached me and said, "I have no money, you must string a garland for me." As per his request to conduct the worship by adorning the Guru's portrait, I strung together Rajamalli flowers and Ashoka leaves and provided it to him. While handing it over after the worship, I had advised, "You should attempt to place our garland first." I had crafted the garland with the intention that each flower should represent a garland. Amidst the list of various organizations and individuals, the garlanding by Swami Nijananda inadvertently became the ninth. Out of curiosity to witness this, I too had gone. However, even as he was being helped down from the train, Nijananda had already placed the garland. Although a major altercation ensued over this, it yielded results. At the conference held at Vasu Talkies the following week, Sadana Mathavu Narayani Amma of Kollam stated, "Does not everyone refer to the Swami as Sree Narayana Guru? Similarly, it is my request that he be addressed as Nataraja Guru, and everyone should accept this." The conference passed the resolution unanimously. At least some individuals in Varkala are aware of this matter.

After his return from America, wherever he sat, tender coconut, bananas, and puffed rice would be placed on a leaf nearby. This was intended as an offering in reverence to the Guru. Many might not have noticed the purpose behind it. Furthermore, he strictly mandated others to perform prostration at his feet. Prior to his departure to America, Nataraja Guru was an individual who rejected such customs. Once he realized his error, he corrected it and ensured that others corrected it as well.

A faction of Dharma Sangham members—nine of them, from Krishnanandan to Ramanandan—objected to the idea of handing over the land near Varkala College to the SNDP. It was Kumaraswami and Swami Ramananda who played the prominent role in conducting the litigation that spanned ten years between the SNDP and the Dharma Sangham. When these nine individuals were expelled from Sivagiri, I was consecutively transferred to seven branch ashrams solely for serving coffee to Kumaraswami, who was one among them. Later, when he won the case and returned, a complaint was raised that I did not accord him proper respect. During the course of this litigation, this Kumaraswami safeguarded the monks by burying the keys and standing guard with a machete for seven years. The ousted Saswathikananda is a relative of that Kumaraswami. Yet, he could not even recall that sorrow. To this day, Sivagiri has not been able to even compile a factual history of these events.

Swami Anandatheerthan primarily handled the legal aspects of the case, and upon its conclusion, he was installed as the President. However, not only was he removed from his position by fabricating false cases, but the then Secretary also had the cunningness to execute a document stating that the thirty acres of land belonging to the Dharma Sangham would automatically become the property of the SNDP if taxes were paid for twelve years.

At that time, Nataraja Guru, Mangalanandan, and Anandatheerthan jointly raised a claim through the *Gurukulam* magazine, questioning why the Dharma Sangham could not manage such a college. In response, some thugs from Varkala gathered at the gates of the Gurukulam and hurled abuses, and since Dayanandan, who had recently joined the Dharma Sangham, directed unmentionable remarks at Nataraja Guru, they withdrew from the initiative.

However, when Anandatheerthan stayed back at Sivagiri and advocated for this cause, these individuals hid in Viswambharan's shop and orchestrated an attack on Anandatheerthan when he stepped out. I am also aware of the history where that case was settled for two thousand rupees. At the time, no one knew who the assailant was. Yet, that very person later cried out from a hospital bed, confessing that his leg had to be amputated because he had assaulted that particular individual. All these facts are known to the current President, Swami Madhavananda. Therefore, I pray for the Guru's blessings and the benevolent wishes of the people so that the Dharma Sangham may continue to exist truly as the Dharma Sangham, and to make the public realize that it is not merely a communal organization.
Birthday Message
August 1988

To rectify the errors that emerged in the novelty of antiquity and the antiquity of novelty, numerous great souls have incarnated on earth across various eras, known by different names such as prophets and avatars. It is evident that they all functioned in accordance with their respective times. When speaking of time, life itself constitutes a temporal span even for an ant. Similarly, for the animal kingdom, life is a dimension of time. This principle applies to everything from a mere blade of grass to the sprawling banyan tree, which achieves the absolute fullness of life within its species. The ancients utilize the banyan tree metaphorically in this exact sense. The fundamental reason for their growth is the presence of life. Contingent upon the variations of space and time, the cycle of growth, sustenance, and destruction is inherent not only in human beings but across all living creatures. Intelligence, too, manifests with distinct variations among them. What is the cause of this?

Plants and trees are uprooted prematurely, and human beings face untimely demise. Those who perish in wars, those who lie waiting for death, and those who end their lives by hanging are all included in this paradigm. This encompasses those who believe that all these possess life, those who believe in the existence or non-existence of the power of sin, the intelligent and the unintelligent, the scientific scholars who consider themselves to have attained the pinnacle of intellect, and above all, the path of action, agency, and execution that operates without instruments or mediums—not merely on this earth but across the nine celestial spheres—directing the essence of the atomic life of the *Panchakoshas* (five sheaths), which has evolved through the five elements and is channeled into the five senses, configuring its distinct nature.
When knowledge becomes subjugated to the lower nature,
A fraction of a second feels like a thousand years.

As stated by Narayana Guru, there can be no doubt for scientific or biological theorists that science would require thousands of years to thoroughly evaluate the virtues and vices of life encompassed within the evolutionary theory of the *Panchakoshas* of life. The process by which such an expansive operation of life creates wonders before humanity, most visibly through the earth, the sun, and the moon, is evident even to the most ignorant. Through the passage of eras, one can deduce that everyone—from demons who possess a subtle understanding of the potential of action extending to *Moola Ganapathi*, the lord of the foundational forces spanning from the elemental entities to the stellar constellations, to the *Vethalas*, the indwelling demigods who have attained the celestial realms, and even up to the holy Trinity (*Trimurti*)—is equally subject to pleasure and sorrow.

The time referred to here is not the time mentioned earlier. The culmination of time occurs in terms of *Manvantaras*. The epoch of one *Manu* is documented as consisting of seventy-one *Chaturyugas*. The seventh *Manvantara* among these is the *Vaivasvata Manvantara*. We are currently in *Kali*, the fourth quarter of its twenty-eighth *Chaturyuga*. The *Dharma* (duty/righteousness) of the *Kaliyuga*, which is considered the fourth quarter (the others being *Satyayuga*, *Tretayuga*, and *Dvaparayuga*), is to contemplate and evaluate the virtues and sins accumulated through the actions of the preceding two *Yugas*, and to execute the actions as ordained by that divine (*Brahman*) resolve. This has been incorporated into the designated karma of the *Shudra* class. The term '*Shudra* class' denotes the ignorant, the despised, the lowly, and the caste-fanatics extending down to the *Chandala*. There was a system of karma that regulated even food consumption. The trajectory of karma that resulted in the categorization of emperors, kings, and Brahmins as the rulers not just of India but of the world, was a modern diversion of this. Although it is stated that the potent trajectory of all these karmas is destined to fall upon the *Shudra*, it is not easy to evaluate and articulate the ignorance that ensues when knowledge and capability fall into the hands of the world's *Chandalas*, who do not even understand for whom this is intended.

This is because, when it fell into the hands of the ignorant *Shudra* class, and the context of the coming together of the Dravidian and the Aryan arose, bringing with it a succession of wars, victories, and defeats akin to karmic prowess, it is not difficult to observe that both the Dravidian and the Aryan equally harmonized their dedication, reliance, karma, and dharma—not merely in India but globally—to attain the true deity of fortune through the traditional system of divine worship. It has been proven that the most suitable lineage for this is the *Shudra* class. A proof of this lies in the divine voice (*Ashariri*) that occurred even prior to Sri Krishna's birth, warning that despite giving birth to him, he should not rule as a subordinate to the emperor. Since the king of that time could not be made to declare this, Krishna demonstrated it through his actions by slaying him and assuming the role of the rightful heir. It is in the sense that Krishna, who stood at the absolute forefront of divine status, embodied every deity, sage, ascetic, active participant, devotee, and prophet who had appeared until then, that the phrase "*Yatra Yatra Yogeshvara Krishna*" is uttered. In the visionary doctrine known as *Yugadharma*, asserting a prominent position, Sri Krishna profoundly and authoritatively expounded upon the duties of the age through the eighteen chapters of the *Gita*, while preceptors, gods, and sages provided an intimation of the future.

Numerous prophets, gurus, and the lineage of the *Parayi Petta Panthirukulam* who came thereafter have vindicated this. It is evident that figures from the more recent past, such as Sri Shankara, Narayana Guru, and Chattampi Swami, emerged with distinct ideological missions. Whether they successfully achieved them or not is beside the point. Sri Shankara propounded Advaita, Madhvacharya advocated Dvaita, and Thiruvalluvar poetically championed the concept of 'One Caste, One Race, One God.' Chattampi Swami authored and completed the *Vedadhikara Nirupanam* to dismantle the ritualistic sections (*Karmakanda*) of the Vedic religion. Narayana Guru functioned practically, striving to elevate humanity through action.

The dharma referred to here is the *Dharma* of the *Kaliyuga*. Whether a *Chandala*, a Brahmin, or anyone in between, the *Shudra* has advanced by acting in a way that makes him forget his own karma, merit, and prowess, which are essential for humans, as well as for the departed sages and gods, to attain liberation and virtue. The ultimate reward for a god or a sage thus far has been liberation. In order for this very same outcome to be realized for the entire *Shudra* class, an act in accordance with divine providence is outlined below. It proclaims a truth that is indispensable not just for a householder, but for absolutely everyone.

The rationalist and the salvation-seeker, stricken by paralysis, are swaying unconsciously after consuming poisonous liquor to the brim. Each of us is a human being embodying moral decay, trying to pose as a scientist or a research scholar. This is because they are petty creatures who mix up the scientific and the unscientific without hesitation, eager to denounce each of the aforementioned. Today's rational beings, operating without distinction between the scholar and the ignorant, losing both *karma* and *dharma*, are like plants uprooted from a gymnasium. Consequently, the scholar, the ignorant, and everyone else caught between them are eradicating their lifespans within this vortex. To escape from this, I am utilizing this occasion to inform you of a clear and resolute matter.

Discovered through states described as ethereal, manifest, and luminous, a path of karmic resolution is taking place here. This path enables one to act and cause others to act benevolently for all living beings in the world, while seeking the cessation of sorrow in my twenty-nine years of life. The *Guru Margam* (Path of the Guru) advised at Santhigiri is the greatest path of resolution, which, through a life of obedience according to the divine will (*Brahmanishchayam*), removes sorrow, brings merit through action, and carefully preserves *dharma* as its foundation. This *dharmic* life, which must be acquired with vigilance, is meant to reach not just humans but all living beings, by making each person enact the chapters of *dharma* that span from the atom to the infinite in the universe, thereby realizing it within oneself. It not only allows us to preserve it in our actions by theorizing the evolutionary paths of the solar system that we previously pervaded, but it has also become capable of achieving the complete realization of the lineage. Its detailed explanation is not to be publicized but only spoken of in person. Informing you that the medium that helps all people, forgetting caste or religion, to arrive at the singular doctrine of humanity is something you can trust and inspire trust in, and wishing you eternal peace so that this auspicious day may benefit you by enabling you to progress through it and, if necessary, making yourself worthy of liberation,
Your Swami
Birthday Message - An Appendix
August 1988
Disciple: What can we, who have no knowledge about such a profound subject,
understand? How can we understand?
Guru: The fact that such a matter exists in the world is known at least to a few among the Hindus.
It has been spoken about a little at a time, on multiple occasions, by various people.
Disciple: Who are they?
Guru: Sri Krishna is the one who comes foremost.
Disciple: What the Guru just said is not entirely clear. It would be helpful if you could
elaborate on it.
Guru: The first evidence is indeed that even before Sri Krishna's birth, Kamsa received

a notification in accordance with the divine will. Along with that, Kamsa felt inclined to deny it because the royal authority of the *Shudra* class lacked humility. Wherever the *Shudra* class has attained royal power, it has been like that.
Disciple: Knowing that he would lose his life upon hearing the ethereal voice, wasn't Kamsa's action a primitive aggression for survival,
rather than a mere denial?
Guru: Once it is seen as divine will, how can it be an aggression for survival?

What Kamsa displayed was something inherent in the oppressive nature of royal authority. The arrogance of not knowing what constitutes the gentle or the virtuous. That is the ignorance of the *Shudra*. Later, Buddhism emerged. It was the *Shudra* class within it who completely denied it with the help of the Brahmins.

During Sri Krishna's time, the state administration was in the hands of the *Shudra*, wasn't it? Even within Sri Krishna's Yadava clan, the lack of humility and wisdom to respect the gentle and the virtuous later surfaced. Isn't making Samba dress as a woman and incurring the sage's curse evidence of this? With that, didn't the Yadava clan fight among themselves and perish?

Wherever you go, you can see that the *Shudra* remains the same even today. Even though Sri Krishna came as such a great personality in the past, and granted that the Brahmins or all these *varnas* glorify Sri Krishna—don't we have good evidence that they still could not truly respect him?
Disciple: Could you elaborate a bit more on the evidence that they did not respect
him?
Guru: Without accepting Sri Krishna's words that those who worship the ancestors go to the ancestral realm, those who worship the deities

go to the realm of deities, and those who worship me will attain me, the Vedic religion was re-established in Sri Krishna temples. Imposing a Vaishnava nature on Sri Krishna, the Vedic religion, which did not hesitate to draw a sacred thread around Sri Krishna's neck, performed all sorts of mockeries here! Can't you guess? As for the clan in which Sri Krishna was born, even though Sri Krishna became a king, they still remain in the status of Harijans today. They have not been able to respect that clan either. In South India, so many people belonging to the Harijan or *Shudra* class held administrative power. Cheraman Perumal was one such person. Pulayanarkotta stands as evidence for that.

I have heard that a fisherwoman whose illness Sri Ramakrishna cured was a woman of royal stature. This woman was a devotee of Kodungallur. Unable to enter temples in Bengal, she came here to Kodungallur. Here, the idol could be seen up close. One day, the Goddess showed her in a dream: "Why do you come here; can't you place me there?" Thus, she immediately had a form of Bhadra sculpted. After it was sculpted, she realized that a Brahmin had to consecrate it, not her. So, she kept the sculpted form safely in a box. She had another dream, instructing her to have Sri Ramakrishna Deva perform the consecration.

This woman fell ill. Her husband was a Brahmin. If a royal woman dies, a Brahmin cannot remain there. Hence, he met Sri Ramakrishna and expressed his sorrow. Within a few days, she recovered. She had vomiting and diarrhea. The Swami caught it. He was bedridden for three months. When such great historical truths exist, why are you asking all this? There would be so many similar things to say.
Disciple: Are you saying it is because of an inability to respect Buddha
Guru: It is not about the inability to respect Buddha. Because he was a king,

everyone accepted him. For instance, Emperor Ashoka allowed his own children to work for the cause. With that, it became the norm that celibates (*Brahmacharis*) could operate anywhere. Buddhism spread in India and abroad. For about eight hundred years, Buddhism remained in power. The followers of the Vedic religion waited. For convenience, some *Shudra Brahmacharis* in Buddhism abandoned their celibacy. Consequently, not only did the people turn against them, but the Kshatriyas and the Brahmins who aligned with them collaborated to use the *Shudra* class itself to beat and drive away Buddhism.

Once the Buddhists retreated, bad rumors spread about them. Many Buddhists were indeed killed. Moreover, in their places of worship, instead of the eulogies of Buddha, they consecrated Bhadrakali and created rituals like *Vela*, *Padayani*, and *Poora-idi*. Don't you know about the offering called *Poora-idi*, where young maidens carry *Thalappoli* around the temple, and they set up mortars and pestles, pound turmeric and charcoal together, and scatter everything around amidst frantic dancing, drumbeats (*chenda*), and a demonic atmosphere? All of these were implemented here by the rulers who came after Shankaracharya.
Disciple: Before Shankaracharya?
Guru: I mentioned earlier that Buddhism existed here for eight hundred years.

Remains of Buddhist *viharas* glorifying the attributes of Buddha have been excavated from many places in Kerala itself. When faced with opposition, those among the followers of Buddha who had wealth, capacity, and resources fled to countries like Ceylon and China.

Then some physicians remained here. The reason is that a physician cannot be created overnight, right? There were also a few administrative personnel. The Ezhavas or Chekavars were the military commanders here, the administrators of that time. Later, untouchability and caste discrimination were introduced and implemented here in order to destroy them.
Disciple: It is said that Shankaracharya created the caste system, right?
Guru: Shankaracharya had to collude in this and do many things.

It was done to prevent the remaining people from being beaten to death. Advaita was introduced with the concept that all should live as the children of one father. However, it was not implemented because it was impossible to step down into the impurity and work. The followers have written extensively to make it appear that the *Varna Dharmas* were prescribed by Sankaracharya. Adi Shankara did not do that.
Disciple: Can it be said that all this was ordained by God?
Guru: No, it was not ordained by God. When there was a lack of people with administrative or martial capabilities, they created untouchability by making the Shudra class fight among themselves.
Disciple: In places like Kannur, Thalassery, and Kozhikode, the Brahmins who embraced Buddhism
were ostracized and degraded. The degraded Brahmins are the Thiyyas. This is what Kerala history states. Is this what the Guru is also saying?

Guru: Exactly that. Later, when the Malabar rebellion occurred, the thugs prepared to harass the Thiyyas. Again, a number of people belonging to their community fled to Coorg. Many men were hacked to death. It was mostly the women who fled.

Thus, the Ezhavas were degraded in every way and transformed into an untouchable caste. Some were included in the Harijan category. The rest became the poor, the farmers, and the physician families. Out of necessity. Those who faced such severe untouchability, those without formal knowledge, became physicians. Sanskrit became their own—how did the Sanskrit of the Brahmins reach those who were considered unapproachable and untouchable? Reading history reveals that physicians emerged among the Nairs only within the last three hundred years. The Nair community itself did not exist. The scholars later wrote and created sixty-four sub-sects within the Nairs themselves. Aren't Valappat Maman Vaidyar and Kakkanat Vaidyar, who came from the Ezhava tradition, renowned? How did this happen?
Disciple: In the olden days, the appellation Harijan did not exist, did it, Guru?
Wasn't it Gandhi who popularized such an appellation?
Guru: Harijan means belonging to Vishnu or belonging to God, doesn't it?
In that sense, weren't those in Krishna's lineage at that time the people of Hari themselves? Weren't the people of Hari left unrespected even then?
Disciple: Wasn't it in the name of Rama that Gandhi surrendered himself and performed his actions?
Guru: Gandhi held firmly to the name of Rama and the concept of Ramarajya.

That was a mistake made by Gandhi. Are not Rama and Ramarajya, which became obsolete due to the Yugadharma (the duty of the age), belonging to the Treta Yuga? As a result of going after worship, Gandhi's mission remained unfulfilled. His organization did not listen to his words. Despite being such a sacrificial figure, not only did India fail to respect or obey that man's words, but he was also shot dead. And that too was done by a Brahmin. If Mahatmaji had been a Brahmin, perhaps he would not have been shot. Is not this much evidence enough to completely expose the statesmanship here?
Disciple: For a moral culture to emerge in a manner suited to the times,
what should be done?
Guru: What must be done has come through Sri Krishna and Buddha.

It has also come through the Parayi petta panthirukulam (the twelve clans born to the Pariah woman). The eighteen Siddhars belonged to all clans, starting from Brahmin, Kshatriya, and Vaishya. Was it not Thiruvalluvar, who said 'Ondre Kulam Oruvane Devan' (One caste, one clan), who belonged to them? The *Thirukkural* of such a Thiruvalluvar stands very strongly as the core of Vedanta. It is also a part of knowledge. With the scholars' method of closing their eyes and creating darkness, isn't all this equivalent to having gone into the dustbin?

In libraries in America and Europe, the Gita, the Bible, and the Quran may hold the first position. Does that mean that Christians in Britain and America as a whole will accept the Quran or the Hindus? Will they obey?
Disciple: Are you suggesting that the public generally enjoys the Gita and the Thirukkural
merely as literary forms?
Guru: What is the doubt in that?
Disciple: Can you suggest a path that can be
followed by humanity as a whole?
Guru: Are not the things that existed in the past
applicable to humanity?
Disciple: Distinct from them, do you have anything to suggest that does not lead to religious hatred
and makes human cooperation more evident?
Guru: In principle, there is something to suggest. If we do not discard it

as we did in the past, an authoritative step towards permanent existence for the entire world is being implemented through our current ideology. Our beginning is from where Narayana Guru, Buddha, and Krishna left off.
Disciple: How is that? I do not understand.
Guru: The Supreme Soul Sri Krishna came and demonstrated something through His actions

before leaving. He demonstrated the matters of the Devas (gods) and the Pitrus (ancestors) and assumed agency for it Himself. That is why it was said, 'Mamekam sharanam vraja' (Surrender to Me alone). He removed the scholars and court poets of that time, as well as Bhishma—who was an expert in archery and attained the bed of arrows—and Drona from this world, and re-established the government itself. He Himself proved that sages and the enlightened are its guides.

The enlightened ones do the very same subject that the sages perfect. They implement it in its entirety. That is why Vyasa, in the language of realization, said, 'Yatra Yogeshwarah Krishnah' (Wherever is Krishna, the Lord of Yoga). The perfect evidence for this is that Krishna took birth as an enlightened being Himself. Another proof is crossing all the states of the Devas, attaining the presence of Ishwara, and stepping into the presence of Brahman. That is the eighth state.

Having understood all this and established the administration, Krishna tells Arjuna that, since the Yadavas themselves ignored the sages, Dwarka itself would sink due to that sinful power. Not only could they not be saved, but they were also going into renunciation. It proves that the Dharma of Kali had begun there. The truth is that, because the birth happened in the Dvapara Yuga, despite doing everything, it could not be completed.

Respecting this, Buddha, who studied all texts, stopped everything else and tried to awaken people by making them chant only 'Buddham Sharanam Gachchami'. It must be an enforcement of the very same thing that the great Thiruvalluvar stated. Sankaracharya, who was elevated in Satva, realized that his caste would not change merely through the study of Puranas and epics. There is a story told about this. It is said that Parvati, in the guise of a Pariah girl, lay on the road wailing, and when he shouted 'Hoy Hoy' to avoid untouchability, the poor woman lamented, 'Son, if you, who are pious and wise, do this, will others touch me? Therefore, lift me from the path and lay me aside.' And accordingly, he moved her. When the frail, bone-like woman felt very heavy, he thought about the reason right there. The story goes that when he recognized her as Parvati, he saw that beauty and wrote the *Soundarya Lahari*. That must be regarding spiritual enlightenment, which is why it is written that when he shouted 'Hoy Hoy', she retorted asking whether it was the body or the soul that should move away. Writers might have fabricated him as an Advaitin. In spirituality, there is only one argument. It might have been done for the survival of the Vaidikas, to satisfy through court poetry, and to maintain the hegemony of the Brahmins. In doing so, the truth might have been forgotten. Human, after all! Mistakes can happen. Intelligent people should understand that.
*Janmana jayate shudrah* (By birth, everyone is a Shudra)
*Karmana jayate dvijah* (By action, one becomes a twice-born)

Is it not shown by all of them through this Gita verse that the time is what the Shudra is entitled to and must achieve through Karma? Has it not been proven that the Shudra lost the ability to understand this? This is exactly what Narayana Guru also did. In order to help the Shudras recognize what Vedic practices and idol installations (Prathishta) are, he gave all of that to them, and then said that none of it is needed anymore and what we need are educational centers. The Murukkumpuzha temple with "Truth, Dharma, Compassion, Empathy" written on it and the Kalavamkodam temple where a mirror was installed, have enlightened us. Despite developing the S.N.D.P. for social growth from the age of thirty to seventy, and abolishing the worship of ghosts and evil spirits, puja rituals, and even the *Kettukalyanam*, they could not understand it because of the severe Shudra nature inherent in them. That is why the Swami had to establish the Dharmasangham. Thinking of the Shudras who had worked until then, he had to regret, "Oh! These poor people will not get this." Even amidst physical ailments, the pain that stood before him was that he could not do anything. When there was no improvement even after the combined treatment of Maman Vaidyar, Olassa Mooss, and Panavally Krishnan Vaidyar, Dr. Samuel was brought in, implying that this treatment was not enough. He evaluated the treatment up to that point and said, "We cannot provide any further treatment beyond this; let us pray for him for five minutes," and then knelt down and prayed with everyone.

When he cried during his Samadhi saying, "I don't have a child," the ignorant devotees of the Swami at that time thought he was grieving over not having a biological child. Thus, the karmic dosha of acting against what the Swami worked for still persists. An explanation of this has been provided in the Santhigiri magazine under the title "The Mistake of Not Knowing What a Guru Is."
Disciple: Then how will the people understand your idea
that is of such magnitude?
Guru: That is why people like you should ask and learn from time to time,

correct it, and put it into practice. This era is suitable for it. What is happening here today can be seen in all the nations of the world. And what happens there can be seen here. Media has expanded that much.
Disciple: Could you indicate how it is put into practice?
Guru: More than what others have shown, as per the divine will (Brahmanischayam), a great capacity
to work for the full period of a Yugadharma has been bestowed upon us as Brahman.
Disciple: Will you explain this and make me understand?
Guru: As you know, I too, like you, had been worshipping in the Trimurti system and,
in particular, served for seventeen years not just at the headquarters of Narayana Guru but at its branches:
Disciple: Could this idea not be introduced and developed through the ideology of
Narayana Guru?
Guru: It is not possible.
Disciple: Why?
Guru: Not only did he work by assimilating everything within the system of idol installation,

but he also established puja rituals and composed hymns and praises. Due to that tradition, the Vedic religion in Kerala has reached a stage where it exists only among the Ezhavas, next to the Brahmins.
Disciple: Cannot the Nairs or other communities belonging to the Shudra varna
adopt this?
Guru: Because the government here fell into the hands of the Nairs in the name of the Brahmins
Disciple: What do you mean by saying that it fell into the hands of the Nairs in the name of the
Brahmins?
Guru: When the Nairs gained administrative power, they engaged in Sambandham (alliances) and absurdities

and became Brahmins. Now they have neither Brahminhood, nor Shudrahood, nor Karma, nor Dharma, nor humility. Due to the complete embodiment of arrogance, they have lost everything. The wisdom to respect and assimilate has also been lost. I have proof for that. One Velupillai Swami from Kottarakkara came to the Aluva Advaita Ashram after a journey. He was a householder and a wealthy man who had set out to become a monk. During prayer time, he was sitting under a mango tree, gazing at nature. A Swami went up to him and asked why he was sitting like that at this time.
"I am a Shudra. I do not want any Ezhava prayers"—was the reply. It is clear that the monk Velupillai Swami did not even know what Varna was.

When they had enough to eat and clothe themselves, they were ready to stand as the king's men. They tried to establish it. The reason is the community itself. That is why that community did not accept Sri Chattampi Swami's *Vedadhikara Nirupanam*—which is entirely a denial of the Vedas, as you know. It is because they could not comprehend the greatness of an Acharya's nature that this happened.
Disciple: Is progress possible without assimilation?
Guru: They will assimilate. They will be made to assimilate. Progress is possible. It is the divine will (Brahmanischayam).
Progress will undoubtedly occur in all actions. There are not just one, but many proofs for that even now.
The great country of India transformed into many islands and then became the continent of Asia.
Disciple: Just as it is said 'Jambudvipe Bharatavarshe', was this entire Asia
a single great country?
Guru: Is that not the reason why the idol of the bull is mentioned in the story of

Moses? Polytheism was prevalent everywhere on this continent. Since Moses's attempt to bring people under a single God could not be stopped, when the king and the army there moved together to stop him and his activities, Moses called his followers and left. It is said that all his followers went after him and reached the shore of the Red Sea, and when he struck it with his staff, the sea gave way, and those who tried to pursue Moses and his followers got trapped in the sea and died. Is this not God's grace, so that knowledge could come into the hands of the Shudra? Moses came more than a thousand years after Krishna.
Disciple: Are you saying that Acharyas arrive specifically in accordance with each
era and place?
Guru: Have not attire, language, and nature already moved in different directions?
How many attires are there in India itself? How many languages? Were there not over sixty languages among six hundred native kings? Is that not still prevalent today?
Disciple: You also indicate that an idea brought forward in accordance with an era should spread to various
parts of the world. We indeed see it spreading like that. However, universal ideas create division among people. What do you say is the reason for this?

Guru: There are two or three reasons. It is said that Indians believe in Karma. But there are quite a few who say that there is no Karma. One group claims that Karma itself is a lie, and there is only a sequence of experiences according to one's own mind. Thus, when they lose their standing in society, each one brings up some idea and hangs onto it. They do not care to see whether that idea has any sustainability.
Disciple: It would be helpful if you provided an example.
Guru: When the Russian regime brought forth a purely brutal imperial system,
the masses rose up to challenge it. It had the glory of bestowing upon not just themselves but the whole world a powerful system that could bring the working class to the forefront.

Consequently, communism gradually spread to China as well. This change destroyed Buddhism there, smashing and dismantling the Buddhist monasteries. No matter how many crores of rupees one has, they cannot be rebuilt today. They existed there with such artistic perfection.

Although this aforementioned imperial power of Britain was nurtured and elevated upon the ideology of Jesus, when their arrogance grew, they were ousted in a manner that would destroy them, retaining the same capitalistic nature and the same ideology. Those who were expelled from other countries as thieves and petty creatures are the ones who have grown into a superpower in America.

Here, for this purpose, a man named Ramasamy Naicker brought the Dravidar Kazhagam into practice in Tamil Nadu. However, in Tamil Nadu where all this was preached, uneducated people are still the majority. Moreover, wherever they are, they toil like two-legged beasts and exhibit the farces typical of Tamil Nadu. They also turned temple worship into a bloody battlefield.
Disciple: I did not understand what you meant by turning temple worship into a bloody battlefield.
Guru: Animal sacrifice (slaughtering of goats and cattle) also existed in Kerala. In Chempazhanthy,

a remote village, in the compound of the house where Narayana Guru was born, there were two temples. Both were Bhadrakali temples. In one of those shrines, a portrait of Narayana Guru is kept and worshipped. The other shrine has been dismantled and kept aside. I do not know what its current condition is.

Swami, for the installation, dug a yard deep, removed the blood-stained soil, filled it with fresh soil, and built a pedestal. Now, Narayana Guru's portrait is placed there. An idol—of Bhadrakali, with a broken thumb—which was made in the style of a *Nalambalam*, has been taken and placed facing north. The other one was handed over to a museum.

No one has revealed that back then, Nairs and Ezhavas had temples in the same compound. The ownership of both these temples was given to Narayana Guru. In the temple premises, there was a common performance stage (*Kalithattu*) for both temples. Two pillars were arranged on both sides of it to lean against. On one side of it, the elder (*Karanavar*) of the Nairs would sit. On the other side, the elder of the Ezhavas. Decisions were taken mutually. Today, that stage is not there. It has been demolished. Isn't this much evidence enough?
Disciple: Didn't you say that we can bring about this idea? If such great

spiritual masters could not achieve this, then how do you opine it can be brought about? Dayananda Saraswati was persecuted for speaking about this subject and was eventually poisoned to death. When preceptors and their ideologies are thus defied and persecuted, especially when not only communal hatred but also ideological conflicts are prevalent, how will this be put into practice?
Guru: None of this seems like a great difficulty. For our idea to be implemented,

a conditional pathway has been given as *Brahman*. It is because that one thing was not realized that previous preceptors, such great scholars, and heads of states were unable to function effectively. That is the sole stumbling block.
Disciple: The preceptors who came before were unable to do this. Could the Guru please
explain that in detail?
Guru: You must have heard—saying 'let the stone split apart,'
the powerful and courageous words of Jesus that would make it split. However, in his final moments, he asked the question, 'Father, have you forsaken me?' Both these have come from the same person.
Disciple: Why did it happen like that?
Guru: In the status of the Trinity, there is a state called the third step. Once

ascended to that state, whatever one sees and hears will seem like the absolute truth. In its light, all these great souls are bewildered and become ready to do anything derived from it. And all of it will happen exactly like that. Once this third stage is completed, until reaching the sixth state, the whole world will be against this Mahatma.
Disciple: Can you explain the reason for that?
Guru: In this world, there exist numerous subtle entities and indwellers.

Proof of this is Jesus saying, 'Satan, get behind me.' It is out of inability to tolerate the devil that he also asks, 'Father, have you forsaken me?' This occurs after the completion of the third stage. The Prophet was driven away with whips and brooms at that time. Where he was driven to, it was as hot as fire. Didn't he return after surviving by roasting and eating the hides of dead animals? Was it not after that he used the statement that *Jinns* rule the world?

In the same position, we too had to experience it as evidence up to the sixth state. Had we desired supernatural powers (*Siddhi*) or something similar back then, you would have seen more people in Santhigiri today than what is seen around Sathya Sai Baba. It was because I somehow possessed the knowledge that *Siddhis* are an obstacle to spiritual growth and that one must complete this life path properly, that we did not leap into pursuing such powers. Yet, some of the disciples of that time had urged me, saying, 'We can easily do all these things, right?'

It is not that I have not done a few things. And they have yielded results. There was an incident of *Chathaneru* (poltergeist stone-throwing) and a fire breaking out inside a concrete building at a house below the Varkala Sree Narayana Mission Hospital. Since the owner of the house was not there that day, his younger brother Mahani, a medicine merchant—anyone can inquire and verify this—informed me about the matter. I sent a letter through him. 'To the dear Chathan, please do not harm these poor people anymore. With love, Karunakara Guru.' This was the content of the letter. I instructed them to read it at all four corners of the house, read it at the doorway with a lit lamp, and then frame it and hang it in the front porch. With that, the stone-throwing stopped. I do not know if it is still there today. There are many such instances. Eventually, I decided I did not want such *Siddhis*.

Later, these kinds of things stopped yielding results. All of this happened within this sixth state. The very person who had visions about this state became estranged and left. They themselves do not know why they got upset. Six or seven people who had good visions left along with him. The locals would certainly believe what people who worked so closely say, wouldn't they? That way too, a bad reputation came about. Thousands of people, even those who had personal experiences, have abused me as if they had lost their senses. This much is my experience. Isn't this much experience enough for a single individual?

Thus, don't we have the practice of worshipping various kinds of mantra-deities among the *Jinns*, as well as *Yogeeshwaran*, ghosts and spirits, up to *Ghandakarnan*? And then the divine emanations up to the Trinity. Aren't they all considered bestowers of salvation?
Disciple: That is what we had thought.
Guru: Hasn't it been proven that they are not? Buddha was given pork as alms in his palms.
Buddha contracted cholera and died. Such a thing happened to such a great soul. Jesus was crucified. He was betrayed through his most trusted disciple.
Disciple: For the tragedies of these great souls, are these subtle-bodied entities powerful enough
to exert influence even through close disciples like Judas?
Guru: Yes, they are absolutely powerful. Narayana Guru's reflections on God
also prove that.
Disciple: Is this capability given to subtle forces by God?
Guru: No.
Disciple: There is a story among Christians. Lucifer is chief among the
angels. The name Lucifer means morning star. The most prominent Lucifer tried to usurp the authority of God Himself. What is the meaning of this story?
Guru: It is not a story; it is true. It was a star capable of shining
brighter than a sun.
In the language of the Hindus, the *Isha Upanishad* says:
The golden vessel covers
The face of truth.
O Pushan, uncover it,
So that I, a practitioner of truth and dharma, may behold it.

That too is this very same light. A light that shines like the radiance produced when sunlight hits the lid of a large golden vessel. However, to see the true dharma, it is instructed to strike and open even that. Just because you see something resembling the sun or the moon, you do not have to revere it.
'Opening it to know the truth' refers to the path of karma that demands the lives of renunciates to be subjected to even greater sacrifice.
Disciple: Could you please clarify that a little more?
Guru: Those fallen yogis (*Yogabhrashtas*) who have reached up to the sixth step, and the yogis who have blindly reached

up to the sixth without knowing the path, as well as their specific powers, are these indwellers. They will not be able to cross the sixth stage. But their radiance will not fade from that state. Errant forms of light will try to misguide a renunciate as well. If a virtuous woman gets cursed, her abilities are not destroyed. However, it is a negative condition. This matter is similar to that.

The *Mandukya Upanishad* explains this very concept in a different language. If a large torch of bound palm leaves (*Kettuchootu*) is lit, and once it is burning well, someone from a distance spins it very rapidly, it will create an illusion of a large circle of fire glowing with that much thickness.
The truth is the bound torch, not the circle of fire. In this manner, great souls have stated and demonstrated many examples for us.
It is those who have almost reached this sixth state who say, 'Upon crossing the six steps and reaching there, one can see Lord Shiva.' Still, the true essence of the subject cannot be expressed.
Disciple: What is the reason for that?
Guru: Only upon reaching the seventh state can one proceed to the divine presence of God.

...can only be entered. Until then, it belongs to the Trimurti system. For example, you know the mistake made by Devendra, who reached up to the sixth level, and the curse of the sage. There, a wise person (Jnani) knows it as a special power attained together by Parashakti, Moola Ganapathi, and Devendra. But it can be corrected only after crossing this stage.
Disciple: Is this why Narayana Guru happened to say, "Ariya thiruvezhuthaarumundothu
vaanum" (chanting the six sacred letters)?
Guru: Yes, that is what is meant by saying it cannot be corrected. Only what is known
can be said. That is exactly what Narayana Guru has said. Great souls cannot lie.
Disciple: Then how are you able to correct and say it?
Guru: I have told you that many times. It was after reaching the seventh
step that words started coming from the light. There is no form in the seventh step. It means names and forms will not remain. Only a few individual forms that have crossed these stages will remain.
Disciple: Who is meant by "certain individual forms"?
Guru: Only some souls who have departed with the desire for liberation will pass through

like this. If they arrive after completing the sixth state, there is a scriptural rule that the soul can progress by doing penance in the realm it has reached. There is no scriptural rule that one can pass through and do such and such things. However, some of the great souls who go like this are allowed to pass through by that compassionate deity - the Brahma Shakti - as rightful heirs to the actions of the transitioning yugas. They will be born at the beginning of this Kali Yuga and at the end of the Dwapara Yuga. Sree Krishna is one of them. Many belonging to that group were born here during those occasions itself. Prophet, Jesus, Moses, Buddha, Shankaracharya, and the Gurus belonging to the lineage of Thiruvalluvar, up to Narayana Guru, were brought with that desire. Because some of them fell into the path of mystical powers (siddhis), the ideology could not advance. This is why Sathya Sai Baba says, "I have no liberation in this birth; it is possible only in the next birth."
Disciple: Cannot Sri Ramakrishna and Vivekananda be included among the previously mentioned
Gurus?
Guru: Sri Ramakrishna and Vivekananda are realized souls (Jnanis). Other than

seeing and speaking about past events, they could not bring forth a new ideology. Even for those who say the existing ones are not enough, although they could not implement the ideology, there is an action (karma) of it within them. It is just that they are unable to implement it because they could not cross the state.
Disciple: Is it possible for demonic forces to ultimately perish or to attain liberation from
their demonic nature?
Guru: It is possible. I have my own proofs for that. For me,

in this same state (the state after crossing the third step), it was all about abuse, quarrels, and beatings. For seven and a half years, nothing remained but sorrow. Before that, intermittently for about ten years too. During such a troubled time, a word was received from the light. I could not describe what kind of light it was or how it was. I still cannot.

The word received was the Akhandanama (unending chant) present here. It was given to two people. One line to one person and the next line to the other. After six months, one of these two left. After a year, the second person also left. About fifty people who had visions, people who received all this and proved it true, and many thousands of other followers like them left; that day I had a feeling, and I said this would happen. Then many in this group stood up and asked, "What about us? What about us? What about us?" Then I said a word like this: "Should you hear about the festival you are going to see? Isn't it enough to see it? Ninety-nine out of a hundred will have gone," I said definitively.

Not only did they leave, but they also made every possible effort to misinform the world in a bad way. When I was getting into a vehicle, they even stopped me, tore my towel, and beat me. (The one who stopped me died somewhere in North India.)

After that, I came to the place where Santhigiri Ashram is currently located in Pothencode. Back then, it was an uninhabited place where no one entered. Nine months after coming here, the sages under the devas and everyone else agreed to function like before. It yielded ten times the result of the past. Muslim women used to come in rows from Pothencode. They were all cured of their diseases. Within a month and a half, all that stopped. The results started decreasing just like before. Behind that, quarrels, hurdles, and cases up to the Crime Branch were created. Then a message was received, "Remove all this." It is about the old order of worship. Those who received it spent three days in fear, not knowing what to do. On the third day, there was a sudden light and a revelation came, "You were worried, weren't you? It doesn't matter. Tell them to quickly have food and come."
Disciple: What was the reason for telling them to have food?
Guru: At dawn that day, a message was received that no one should drink even cold

water today, and no one should go outside the compound. But someone who came from outside drew water and drank it without listening to what was said. Like algae in a dried-up paddy field, that girl of about seventeen vomited and fainted. She was then given holy water and sacred ash.

Two young men went outside. There used to be a mango tree at the place where the car shed is today. They both got beaten at the base of it. It is not known who beat them. They came back and reported the incident. Everyone started praying as if crying and calling out. There was an instruction to plaster cow dung around the vessel in which food was cooked. Again at five o'clock, there was light. From it, a word emerged - an ethereal voice was heard, "Bathe quickly and have food, I will come again at six o'clock."

Three ailments were cured that very day. The rest were cured over four days. Pattalam Ramakrishnan who was possessed by a Gandharva, a woman possessed by an Esakki, and another woman possessed by a Brahma Preta were still remaining.

"Let this stay there, we will cure it later," a word was received. Then a large group of Acharyas and Devas came. It was written up to three hundred and fifty crores. Then left unwritten. Between four thousand and ten thousand crores are under two thousand four hundred and forty-four Gurus. The count cannot be completely told. All the ailments were cured by the seventeenth day.

A word was received to start the journey. The Brahma Preta alone would not leave. According to the instruction to travel, when the journey started, it came in front and made faces. Gathering all strength, I struck the possessed woman once with my hand. That woman fell over. It has never happened again since then. There were four of us on this journey in the ascetic (Avadhuta) way of life. Chidambaram is the most powerful place in South India. We went there too. We knew beforehand what was at each place. All this gives a vision beforehand. If it is during the time of Puja - "You can enter a little later. The power receiving worship inside will have to move from there" - that is why it is said so. This happened at Chidambaram too. Since then, no temple visits have been made so far. That is when it was understood that there is nothing for me to gain from this Trimurti position.

Then I was told to remain silent for four and a half years. After that, I had to spend another two and a half years like that. Certain things can be done. Certain things should not be done. During these seven years, 'Poortheekaranam' (completion) happened thirty-seven times. Those who came for the prayers held in the name of 'Poortheekaranam' often could go home only after four, five, or seven days. By walking and praying, the stones around the prayer hall loosened and piled up.

Days like twenty-one, ten, fourteen are mentioned as the count. There are instances where it extended up to twenty-seven days. Due to the power of this prayer, a few odd days would be reduced. Saying, "It is completed, you have prayed sincerely," a sign would also be shown in a way that convinced everyone. It was after that, the action (karma) currently happening could be performed.
Disciple: What is this action?
Guru: It is because of this action that we are able to say the word that we
can do it.

These inner controllers (Antaryamis) will not stay if confined in the form of worship. They are moving around as crores of inner controllers. They will not allow crossing the six stages and going beyond.
Disciple: Is that the reason why these Acharyas had to face all these
difficulties?
Guru: No one has been spared.
Disciple: What does that mean?
Guru: No one who crosses the three stages has been spared. When one grows a beard and hair

and walks around according to their respective religious customs, the common people who see them assume that they are great Siddhas or liberated souls. That is not true. They might not have even crossed the third stage. Only a master who has crossed that stage can help another cross it. Those who do not find such masters will develop an inexplicable hallucination stemming from the overconfidence of having attained this light and vision. They will roam around like various kinds of lunatics and like people observing different kinds of ascetic vows. Since some people experience benefits from them and others suffer the greatest harm, the public will be unable to distinguish right from wrong.
My own Guru helped me cross up to the fourth stage. It was Lord Krishna who appeared after seven and a half years to help me cross that. Lord Krishna's stage is the eighth.
Disciple: Is it not true that some people have the experience
of seeing the Guru's form in the form of Lord Krishna?
Guru: Lord Krishna was my Guru in many births. That very same Guru

helped me cross in this birth as well. Those who have helped cross will also come up to the point that has been crossed. That is why it is said that one can cross over while remaining in the body or from the ethereal realm.
Disciple: Having come to guide this world, the world
is unable to absorb this. Why is that?
Guru: Are they not people who are accustomed to

various paths—those of prophets and deities? They cannot suddenly absorb something new. Moreover, the demonic nature of those who lived and died as nobodies exists in the subtle realm. And then there are millions of fallen yogis (*Yogabhrashtas*).
Disciple: Do fallen yogis still exist today?
Guru: Absolutely, they do exist. Men who have grown their hair like women, women who have taken up

false asceticism. There will be many such people. The Bhagavatam mentions this in its description of the Kali Yuga. Among the hundreds of thousands in this group, there might truly be only one or two genuine ones. Some will get lost in their supernatural powers (*Siddhis*). A few people will become engrossed in worshiping their chosen deity and get lost in that. A few people will display their knowledge and its enlightenment, pretending to be heads of monasteries, and having power bestowed upon them by the people. This would be akin to a large library falling into the water. All these people will show more than what they possess and will either lose their way or lead others astray in some manner. Eventually, they will become fallen yogis and inner dwellers.
Disciple: Are you saying that such fallen yogis
truly still exist today?
Guru: Yes, they absolutely do exist. In addition to this, there is another category of

fallen yogis. I will mention someone from my own experience regarding this. Kalladi Masthan. I have had respect and affection for his tradition of wisdom. I had heard about his supernatural powers and wisdom even before meeting him. Thus, I was very eager to see him.

Guru Pathani Swami and I used to sleep under the Valiyathura bridge, which was under construction at that time. From there, we would walk southwards towards the Poonthura beach, conversing about various matters. We would walk like this, occasionally resting at certain spots, sleeping on the beach after brushing away the surface sand, walking again, and sitting in the fishermen's huts used for storing nets when it rained.

There is more wealth in the sea than what can be taken from the land. People do not know that. The wealth in the sea will never run out. It might get exhausted on land. Pathani Swami would say many such things, as well as matters concerning ascetics. Occasionally, he would tell me to look into the depths of the sea and ask me to sit. Once the meditation became steady, what I would then see was the interior of the sea. I could see indescribable animal-like creatures and numerous mountains beneath the ocean, akin to Agasthyarkoodam in our eastern region. If those without experience in such visions were to see this, they might tremble with fear and even lose their lives. One could see creatures approximately a furlong in length and half a furlong in width. I do not know if they were fish. They would swallow numerous creatures, like sea snakes. If caught in their mouths, nothing could escape. However, some smaller creatures could also be seen alongside them. That is, creatures the size of sharks. If two or three creatures of this species stood together, the larger ones would not approach them. If they stood alone, they would approach. For example, a KSRTC bus would take some time to take a turn. Within that time, a small auto-rickshaw would have completed sixteen circles. This is just like that.
It is impossible to describe the myriad colors and types of fish that exist; they can only survive up to a hundred feet below the surface. Very small fish are not seen at the bottom either.

The Guru explained that the smaller ones cannot withstand the pressure at the bottom. The colors of the fish cannot be described. The naked eye cannot see their true colors. My experience is that objects seen with the physical eye appear much brighter in subtle vision. The capabilities of the external eyes have limits.
While living like this, the Guru said one day: "You should go up to the Sannidhanam and come back." By Sannidhanam, the Guru meant Beemapally. When I go like this, I only return when I feel like it.
Upon reaching the gates of Beemapally, I saw Kalladi Masthan. I recognized him from what I had heard. At that time, there were many people who respected him.
Masthan was squatting on the shop-front of a betel-shop owner named Muhammad. It was his habit to grab handfuls of peanuts from his peanut jar, chew them, and spit them inside the glass cabinet.

If anyone went there, he would throw and smash a large soda bottle. No matter what he did, Muhammad would just sit bent over, rolling beedis. He felt that doing all this was an act of grace towards him. Moreover, Masthan would not take such liberties in anyone else's shop.

As soon as I recognized the person, I bought a tea and brought it to him. Immediately, he took water from Muhammad's lemon-water pot, rinsed his mouth, and extending both hands, took the tea and drank it in two gulps. He drank it to the last drop without wasting any. I bought a banana for two annas, placed it there, and returned. For some reason, I did not feel like staying there at that moment. I went straight to the Kunnupara temple.

When I returned the next morning, that shop was closed. I only had one anna in my hand. I gave it and bought a tea. The moment I entered the shop, Kalladi Masthan sat with his hand extended.
