As soon as I handed over the tea, he drank a mouthful and then stirred his tongue in that tea. He licked the brim, the bottom, and all four sides of the glass.

In the meantime, he sang praises in Urdu. I could not understand what it was. After that, he hugged me and made me drink that half-consumed tea. Having never eaten leftover food from anyone—not even from my mother—until that day, I felt like drinking it, and I drank it. He snatched the glass from my hand and threw it far away. Holding me by both my shoulders, he kept me at a distance, sang praises in Urdu, and kissed my head twenty times. Since I did not know Urdu, I thought he was speaking in Hindi.

I said, "Babuji, I do not know Hindi." Calling out "Appa," he then began praising in Tamil. Then I started to understand. He repeated this many times. "O one who was born as a king in ancient times..." the hymns of praise went on like this.
From that, I realized that the assertion in Islam that there is no rebirth is a superstition. I was also able to witness and understand this later. He just kept singing.
Taking how many, how many births
Becoming a monk how many, how many times
O one who ruled the kingdom how many, how many times...

The song went on like this. I could not comprehend any of the complex Tamil. Finally, he said, "Everything is there, it is there in abundance"; saying this three times, he gave a push. Just like how he threw the glass. Even though I fell, nothing happened to me. All the fishermen who had come to drink tea gathered around.

"Where did this guy come from? He has also come to Baba, and Baba knows him. He has come precisely for this. Even though we have been sitting here, Baba hasn't even looked at us"—the crowd opined like this.

I experienced an even greater wonder than that. I came to the Guru and narrated everything that had happened. Remaining silent until I finished, he said, "He has given you everything that was meant to be given. And a bit more. He will not let you get close to him anymore."

I was convinced of that truth. After that, I have seen him a hundred times. Every time, I would buy him tea. Upon seeing me, he would turn away and murmur something in Urdu. He wouldn't even take the tea. Until his samadhi, he didn't let me come close. This is an experience that surprised me.

"There is a little meanness. You will get rid of it," said Pathani Swami. This was experienced only after his and my Guru's samadhi. I had a few visions. While they were alive, Pushpangadan Vakil, who ran the Sivagiri dining hall, his younger brother Sundaresan, and I went to Beemapally. Kalladi Masthan took off the torn rag he was wearing—which in the language of cabaret dancers was just a torn cloth—and handed it to Pushpan. I immediately went into a shop and bought him a kaili. He wore it. The taken-off cloth was wrapped up and kept safely. Meanwhile, Pushpangadan and I traveled to Maruthvamala and many other places. It was during this time that both of us together built the ashram in Pothencode.
Disciple: Did Swami stay in Pothencode itself after that?
Guru: No. Went back to Varkala. Stayed there itself.
Disciple: Who looked after this place then?
Guru: The neighbors, today's Appu Swami, Divaka-
ran who died by consuming poison, Sasi, and Bhaskara Panicker's children were the ones lighting the lamps. Janardhanan Pillai, who lived nearby, looked after other matters.
Disciple: Why did this Appu Swami leave later?
Guru: I was not here, right. His desire for sannyasa intensified. Then

he came to Varkala and told me about some minor experiences he had. He said he wished to take up sannyasa and asked me to tell him where to go. He said, "I have a family temple in Njekkad. It is a testing place, and my desire is to stay there."
I forbade him, saying it was not good. He would end up in a helpless situation where he couldn't move away from deity worship. I suggested the names of three or four ashrams.

Apart from the Sree Narayana Mission, there is the Sri Ramakrishna Mission. There are no experiences anywhere there. I have experience with Ramadas Ashram in Kanhangad. There is Sivananda Ashram in Vatakara. There is Brahmananda Ashram in Alathur. Kalappara Sivananda has an ashram in Neyyattinkara. It is a branch of the Siddhashram in Vatakara. I have been able to meet some experienced seekers from there. Even if they don't possess immense wisdom, it is better. Yoga is their discipline. I told him that his disciple, a younger brother named Narayanan, is in Thiruvananthapuram.
He left saying, "I will go to the family temple first and then proceed to one of the places you suggested."

Later, when he returned after ten years, it was a time when I had arrived at Pothencode. There is an ashram in Kallikkad. There is a forge. They work there and also conduct bhajans. Believers come there. There is an ashram here too. He invited me to visit there. Since he couldn't see me at the agreed time, he told Thankappan to inform me that he was waiting.

So I went. He had bought and kept a towel for me to sit on. A small southern extension-like structure was built there. During our casual conversation, I told him, "This will get better, this condition will change—just be careful," and then I left. We haven't met since then.

Around that time, I learned that he spoke highly of me to those who went there. Now, I have come to know that he is speaking the exact opposite with the same tongue. I also heard that he used some derogatory words to those who went from here.

Let me continue what I was saying. I told you that I had some visions. From them, I understood that certain demonic forces were standing in my way to mislead me. One of them was the form of Kalladi Masthan. I felt that it had possessed Pushpangadan. That very day, upon reaching Varkala, I called Pushpan, explained the matter, made him bring Masthan's cloth, and together we threw it into the water under the Poovampara bridge. Anyone can verify this by asking Pushpangadan Vakil in Varkala.

Even after that, Pushpan behaved as if he was not quite well. I didn't question any of this. Whoever connected with me approaches Kalladi Masthan, this demonic force will do something to lead them astray.

It was then that my Guru's words—"He has given some demonic nature, which you will discard"—made sense to me. I could only understand it after thirteen years; the words of great souls have long-term effects.
I know many people like this Kalladi Masthan. They are all lying like those who have fallen into a trap. Even though my Guru told me about it then, I was convinced of it only after this experience.
When I stayed in Neyyattinkara, I saw many people like Kesavan Sanyasi, Vatti Swami, Chatti Swami, Chunnampu Swami, Mannenna Swami, Kudil Swami, and Sambrani Swami.

Another place is Samadhithoppu, a place people believe is still running well today. Then there is Mayiyamma in Kanyakumari. All these belong to a chain of fallacies of this kind. Kompa Swami, who showed many siddhis, also falls into this category. He attained samadhi in seven places.

When my Guru sat with me and other disciples on the veranda of the Thuckalay Munsiff Court, he used to criticize all this. I didn't understand it then. I believe the others with me didn't understand it either. When starting to talk about Kattuva Sahib Mala, Swami used to mention all these things. My Guru's words back then—that all these are stuck at a crossroads and cannot move forward from there—are clear to me today. Only today have I understood its completeness and who the Guru truly is.
Yet, I recall my Guru saying that even he couldn't get me completely in his final days. This path is like an ocean. It should not be forgotten that people believed, loved, and respected all of them.
Among this group, there are some who undergo transformation through the knowledge tradition, like Thuckalay Peerukannu Sahib and Gunamkudi Masthan, who went to Mecca and attained samadhi.
You might think that this sounds like speaking ill of such great men.
Disciple: We don't think like that.
Guru: If not you, someone else will think so. You should think like that.

I believe it is good to think. Because my desire today is that no one else should fall into the trap I fell into. Just like other people, I also used to see all this as the truth. The secret of the "indwellers" (Antaryamis) is this.
Those who show siddhis are displaying the functional capacity of misguided indwellers. As mentioned earlier, there are ten thousand crores under a single Acharya. All of them, when visionaries comeٹ
Disciple: Who is referred to as a visionary?
Guru: Visionary - there are five Acharyas for an era (Yuga). When a Chaturyuga
is completed, only twenty-one Gurus in total come within these twelve thousand divine years.

The remaining karma yogis, yogis, devotees, and their followers will act as indwellers under a Guru who has fallen from yoga, and they will mislead and confuse the great souls who pass by in the aforementioned manner. Millions of such indwellers will emerge, uncountable in number. This is why great souls like Thiruvalluvar say, "Even if one learns a billion scriptures / past lives happen again and again."

Once these twenty-one Acharyas are complete, they teach how to follow the Yugadharma. Five Acharyas will come for each Yuga. Twenty-one Acharyas arrive within the twelve thousand divine years of a Chaturyuga. They are the Gurus of the passing ages.
Disciple: How did you get this knowledge?
Guru: I told you, Krishna is the final Guru. He was

waiting for a soul that had come without losing its way. Nothing can be done without reaching this position. He came in the Dwapara Yuga, didn't he? He cannot step down here either. He is the one who completed that task for me.
The first to arrive was Shirdi Sai Baba. He possessed immense ascetic power. He did not step aside. On the eighth day, he had to be removed. Sree Krishna was doing it.
When Shankaracharya arrived along with his lineage, it was said that he is a renunciate and let him remain there. He stayed for seven days, and then left.
Sree Krishna then told those performing the karma to seek their Guru and act accordingly. He also said that if they could not manage it, they could come back.

Krishna came on the seventh day itself. He told them to rely on their Guru and perform the rituals. They did so, and it was successful. He told them to continue doing it in the same manner and left. That is how they were able to resolve issues, regardless of which *Antaryami* (inner controller) appeared.

Many of the present *Antaryamis* are widely worshipped. They cannot be easily displaced. The divine will (*Brahmanishchayam*) has not granted permission for that. If they harm us, they can be removed. If the individuals they harm come forward, they can be removed. They can be displaced by having those individuals perform the karma again. Otherwise, only if people move away from their beliefs can the *Antaryamis*, who are the objects of their faith, be removed. If they return to their old beliefs after the removal, things will go back to how they were. That is why it is said that one must never disobey the word of the Guru. If disobeyed, every action they take thereafter will go wrong. This is the primary reason for saying that one must not go astray after joining the movement or becoming part of the lineage.
They do not comprehend the vastness of this concept. That is why they end up committing this mistake.
Disciple: Is this what is referred to as *Guruninda* (disrespecting the Guru)?

Guru: This is the gravest form of *Guruninda*. Besides this, *Guruninda* often occurs in many ways through words and actions. In the *Guru Gita*, Lord Shiva advises Goddess Parvathi that if Shiva gets angry, the Guru can save you, but if the Guru gets angry, there will be no one to save you. Sometimes, it may take up to three hundred and fifty years to reclaim what is good. It cannot be seen immediately.
Disciple: Why is it so?

Guru: Well, due to the purification happening here, the minor ancestors (*Pithrus*) will attain rebirth within twelve years. Most likely within the same family. That is the special characteristic of children born after 1973. Every twelve years, the greatness of the soul that is born increases.
During these three hundred and fifty years, highly revered *Acharyas* (spiritual teachers) will be born only occasionally.

After three hundred and fifty years, the lineage will be completed. Many of these *Acharyas* will have been born by then. Thereafter, no other lineages will be able to function without being part of this lineage.
Guruvani
September 1988

I started speaking only after the age of nine. I studied in an *Ezhuthupallikoodam* (traditional village school). Thus, the only knowledge I acquired was what the *Ashan* (teacher) taught me. Otherwise, I never went to a regular school. The *Ashan* kept me there until I was fourteen. By the time we reached the *Siddharoopam* (basic Sanskrit grammar text), the *Ashan* became physically weak. Therefore, I left that place. I did not study anything after that. Subsequently, it was the *Ashan* himself who took me to the Kalady Ashram. At that time, Swami Agamananda was teaching the *Brahma Sutras* to a person named Swami Jagadiswarananda. After passing the Shastri examination from our region, as he was traveling to North India, a person named Swami Madhavananda in Karnataka took him under his wing and taught him. He lived in Benares for twenty-one years. He had the ability to effortlessly recite texts like the *Siddhanta Kaumudi* fluently, back and forth.

I asked him about this, linking it with my own experience. He replied, "Alas, my child, all of this exists. Although the scriptures state the truth, I have not even seen the light of a lit incense stick. So, I cannot speak about it." I asked many people in this manner. I did not get any evidence from anyone. Later, I met a Pathani Swami. It was from him that I could understand this. Based on his advice, I realized that whatever names exist in this world, they all genuinely exist. If we, consciously or unconsciously, utter a name or conceptualize something, it exists. However, humans have not learned where and how to utilize it. This is what I gathered from my own knowledge.

One can worship using the knowledge up to the *Trimoorthi* (Trinity) system, and one can even see its physical manifestations without any distortion using their naked eyes. There is no need to doubt it. Have I not seen and realized it myself? I have no reason to doubt. Its sub-deities, and even ghosts and spirits (*Bhoota-Pretha-Pishachas*), are real. But we have never contemplated what they can do, or what we should do about them. That is, we have not thought about the *Dharma* (duty/nature) of Kali Yuga.

If Kali Yuga has its own *Dharma*, it belongs to the Shudra. Many *Brahma-jnanis* (knowers of Brahman) have emerged among the Shudras. Sree Krishna is the evidence for that. He belonged to the Yadava clan, didn't he! The history of the Yadavas not only spread among us, but we preserve it tightly even today. Then came the *Parayi Petta Panthirukulam* (the twelve tribes born to a Pariah woman). In the meantime, the eighteen Siddhars also joined in. We have not been able to unite any of these and transmit them through a single language or form, as one unified Indian tradition. We call ourselves Hindus. What we have done so far is behave from behind a system that has been transmitted in such a fragmented way—where small castes have minor gods and upper castes have major gods—making it impossible for us to stand united and pass it on.
Justice Krishna Iyer: What should be done now? Do we need a Vishva Hindu movement?
Guru: Not just Vishva Hindu; whether one is a Christian, a Jain,
or a Buddhist, aren't they all the children of India? We must be able to function with the understanding that everyone is a child of India.
Justice Krishna Iyer: That is a materialistic concept.
Guru: It is not purely materialistic; if we do not approach it spiritually as well, where will our
karma lead us?
A Disciple: Isn't it because of our own shortcomings that people became Christians and Muslims?
Justice Krishna Iyer: Yes.
A Disciple: The shortcomings within us must change.
Justice Krishna Iyer: Yes. First, we must identify the shortcomings within ourselves.
Guru: I have already spoken about the shortcomings in my own way earlier!

About establishing minor deities. How can we transform this karma associated with the *Pithrus* who are caught in such minor worship practices, and similarly the *Yakshis*, *Gandharvas*, *Kinnaras*, or what the scriptures call *Vethala Nagaram*? You referred to it here as materialistic. Agreed. But only after traversing that can we move forward, right? What we call *Atmadarshana* (Self-realization) — shouldn't one be freed from this form?
Justice Krishna Iyer: What is the path toward it from here?
Guru: What we have here is the *Gurumarga* (Path of the Guru). When we speak of the Guru, we must conceptualize

everything starting from the *Bhootaganas* (elemental spirits). Even for the *Bhootaganas*, there must be a special power in the atmosphere to govern them. What is the technical obstacle of an atom? How can anyone other than a perfect spiritual seeker (*Athmavadi*) guide this process, by discovering the inherent special power of the inner soul (*Antaratma*) that must be liberated, and through it, achieving the fulfillment of karma?
Guruvani
October 1988

When we talk about the material and the spiritual, aren't we merely speaking of two sides of the same coin? Then why is the material portrayed as something so magnificent? We should not call it entirely bad; nor should we elevate the spiritual and call it perfectly good. One is just the flip side of the other. I do not know what science is. But I have seen it. That is the only way it can be expressed. Only if I were someone who had studied scriptures could I speak about them, right? I can calculate and explain. My focus is not on what is material and what is spiritual. Where do the karmic bonds generated through our way of life stand? Where do they go wrong, and where do they not? What is the reason for it? What lies in the trajectory of karma? Where is its merit (*Punya*)? What is the *Shikhi* (fire/power) that has operated on its ancestral (*Pithru*) side? That is all I know. It will never say anything wrong. There is no point in saying anything else. The scriptural doctrine that the world today functions strictly based on this remains completely true. No matter who says what, no one can claim that this is incorrect.

This is my experience. I am merely stating the qualifications related to my path of karma, my understanding of dharma shastra, and my truthfulness. Many others may have various qualifications. I do not deny that. Nor do I say it is not so. Should we not see what the nature of the soul is, which extends from the elements to the constellations? Otherwise, there is no truth in it. It can be scientifically proven only if we study whether our form ceases to exist at that point. I am simply stating what I have seen and discovered, exactly as it is.

There is a system in which the nine planets, twelve zodiac signs, and twenty-seven stars operate! Our self-realization is the ability to see how it is made to function. Otherwise, there is no point in merely saying that it was like this or like that.

What must be studied first is the special power of the sun that causes the lunar dust particles to fall to the earth, and the karmic path of the earth which is a component of it. How easy is it to just say that it does not exist? I am not speaking from what I have studied; I have seen it. I can only explain it if such a person comes to me. I will speak only if someone asks what evidence exists in a particular part and what should be done with that evidence. Otherwise, I have not acquired the knowledge to compile and expound upon the scriptures.
J. Krishnayyar: Whichever path humans travel, they must ultimately die
—in a sense. They must die partially. What is the state beyond that? Remembering again, remembering again, it goes on like that. Will it go beyond that in such a manner?
Guru: It will only go that way if one works with a goal. Being human,
if one acts like an animal, will it not grow without a goal?
J. Krishnayyar: Is there any research on this subject happening
here?
Guru: It is happening here. It is an experience. That experience

is shared by many people here. They have been able to realize the experience even in their material lives. They have learned to speak about it authoritatively. There have also been quite a few boys like that. If they make a slight mistake, it will deviate. It will not sustain then. No one has truly worked to achieve it according to expectations. I believe it is due to their lack of desire or a deficiency in their karmic capacity. It is this kind of 'research' that is taking place here.

How do the life paths operate in various ways up to the constellations; how should those souls attain liberation, or if they are to be destroyed, how should they be destroyed; if the deity they worshipped needs to be given liberation, how is that done? We have attained the knowledge to do all these things as well. If this knowledge did not exist, we would have had to stand with those who say there is no karmic path and those who say there is no such thing as self-realization.
Everything is according to our conception. Isn't everything a concept! That is why it is said that concept is the karmic mind.

Now, if one was born in a certain lifetime—what was the nature of a snake? What has it become now from that birth of a snake? As an animal! How did it come to be? What was its capacity for action then? What is the reason for those karmas rising like this? Or what is the reason for saying that a human being will return as an animal? This must be recognized. Just one side is not enough; all sides must be known. As one continues to know this, it will become clear what that soul was. This is how it should be understood. What was it? In what form did it manifest? How did that atom operate? By what color is it distinguished? It has been divided into nine, and all that we see is the manifestation of these nine. Just as the same color can be slightly separated and distinguished, our thoughts and feelings themselves can be separated.
Guruvani
November 1988

We are expanding the stream of light of our mind. Not according to the calculations stated by the yogis. By developing it, I have been able to see what that karmic path is, which grows the inner connection (the Kundalini power) from the triangular shape to the thousand-petaled lotus. It is a manifestation of the success of life. That applies only to an individual. It is what is called Kundalini power according to yogic principles. When it reaches the Manipuraka chakra, its shape and nature change. By then, all types of colors would have combined and acted together. In this world, the atomic penetration of everything of all kinds can be seen. This is the realm of the atom. We can see the special operation of these atoms functioning together with blood, flesh, and marrow. It is explained using color itself. Divinity comes only if a particular color is joined. It is not in another. The element of darkness will be mixed in that. In the other, the element of light will be mixed. To specify a certain light, when a vision is completed, for a state to be fulfilled, knowing it entirely in its gross, subtle, causal, and effectual aspects, seven thousand four hundred and forty-four visions must occur. The completion of seven such stages is the divine presence. How can this be explained now?

This cannot be discovered by science. The reason is that science has not grown to that extent. I am not saying this to deny that science exists. Science has simply not evolved enough. How many people can do this? They will break down when they reach that point. A scientist can only reach the complete form of research envisioned by a scientific discipline, right? Thinking beyond that, wasn't there a science here that executed things through the nine planets, operated within the twelve zodiac signs, discovered its calculations to give to us, reached out to the stars, and repeatedly explained to us the innate qualities that reach us up to their fractional calculations? That very calculation is what is being discussed here. It should not be misstated.

In this manner, only an authoritative Guru who has ascended to the position of Devendra, or to the position of the Lord of the Ganas (it is said that Ganapathi has the root authority for this), through the karmic path that has grown up to the Trimurti system, can explain all this. What is the authority of Mula Ganapathi? Or, to what extent does the karma of the state called Parashakti reach in that position? How minutely and scientifically has all this been realized. It needs to be known by further refining and consolidating it. Only then can we be convinced of its evolution. Otherwise, it will not be comprehended.

A karma I perform here to change this—for example, someone says they have a disease. Is the disease real or not? It is real. Then what is the cause? There is no effect without a cause, is there? When discovering the cause, if it came through their karmic path, it is that. Or, if it came through their ancestors, it is that. Or else, if it came through their family worship, it is thus. Categorizing it in this way, the karma that needs to be performed by this person will be made to be done by them alone. Only such fully completed karma will take hold here. When it takes hold, there will be the pain of karma in their body. It will be in the body as well. It will also reflect in their actions. It will happen. After that, if they desire self-realization, they will be guided on that path. Speaking of it is useful only if they have the right to it. Even if not, this can be told to some people. Because it relies on their desires. When desire increases, that increase will affect the karmic path functioning within.

Knowledge is being able to tell what karmic path should operate in any person upon seeing them. That karma will aid in liberation. There is no doubt. Each of us has a karmic path right from birth. How does that come about? Shakta, Shaiva, Vaishnava—these are worshipped as divine, aren't they! Until reaching Advaita, one can only function according to this, right? Advaita is something else entirely. What should one do as long as they are in Dwaita (duality)? Is it right to reject Dwaita? Dwaita cannot be denied. It can be discarded after that knowledge is attained.

Where will the aspect that people comprehend as *Maya* ultimately lead? Must one not attain the state of Agastya, who reached the position of self-illumination? Can this be achieved through mere words? It requires concerted effort. Only such deliberate action can yield results. One must inevitably undertake this *karma*. An individual must independently determine the course of their *karma* and *dharma*. This cannot be decided by another. Therefore, a center of knowledge dedicated to this is essential here.
Guruvani
December 1988

We must be cautious of the nature that manifests in various forms such as mischief, glory, love, devotion, and action. We must safeguard our minds. It will take a considerable amount of time just to understand this. This is precisely because our parents or ancestors were not perfect. Their actions and moral principles will affect us to some extent. This is because nature cultivates blood, marrow, and flesh not just in them and us, but in a way that sustains all living beings in the world. It is transmitted to all living beings in their respective natures. There are also transformations for all these. Every thinker has a distinct perspective on all this. This grass—what is it! How many varieties, and similarly, how many species of birds and animals! All of these possess stomachs, functional capacities, and blood vessels. What is this system that operates everything in perfect equilibrium? Similarly, through the magnitude of what great scientists have discovered, it is possible to fly to many places. Even if all that is true, there will still remain millions and billions of things yet to be known in this world, even if countless discoveries are made. If there is a change in this atmospheric nature or the nature of the solar system, how will we know? We are only capable of acknowledging what we already know as good, known, or heard.

The world is like this. How does it permeate within us? This is what we must consider next. When reflecting thus, among those we consider father, mother, husband, or wife—what lineage have they upheld in this? Under the influence of what inherent tendencies (*vasanas*) have they presented themselves? We must clearly explain this to every child, especially the children studying here. You are not making them understand in that manner. The reason is that you lack such inclinations. The first thing to instill in these children is that you yourself must convince them of the flaws and shortcomings of their parents. Then, what are the circumstances of our home and the circumstances of our ancestors? First, they must be made to understand that. Following that, one must be prepared to confess one's own faults. Who should be prepared? The teachers. I too have several faults. But they are not appropriate to be mentioned now; hence, I am not stating them; they must be told someday. Only then will they comprehend what you teach. Thus, the teacher was able to admit that their father, mother, themselves, and their lineage have faults! That mind is expansive. Therefore, the teacher is worthy of respect. This is being communicated to them for the purpose of cultivating a practice of teaching them in this manner. Otherwise, they will mimic and magnify the antics displayed before them by men and women. No matter how much is said, they will exhibit it. Make this a practice here—our primary task is to encourage them to confess their faults, to observe the misfortunes of their lineage, to repent, and to instill a determination in them to resolve it. The realization should not merely be that one's father, mother, and lineage are at fault and how one can resolve it, but that there are collective flaws spanning from all living beings to the human race. First, make them contemplate how we should perceive this fault. Thus, it should be imparted to children as small, digestible topics. It must also be established that these are the distinct qualities inherent in life, and stopped there. Otherwise, it will veer into Vedanta, and if it moves towards Vedanta, these children will also delve into Vedanta. Vedanta is entirely rationalism. Although some may argue that rationalism is good, it is not. Why? Through rationalism, using intellect, things beyond comprehension will be introduced. Secondly, one might attempt to analyze expansively, thinking, 'Given my parents' condition, I am unlikely to possess this much intellect—yet I have this much intellect.'

This must be communicated to the children first. Only then will a contemplation about themselves be beneficial to them. If this is instilled early on in students, they will subsequently begin to study about something or someone. They will also study about writers. When learning about writers, the children will realize that what they have written is not derived from practical experience, but is imagination. That is a significant achievement. Subsequently, they will learn about certain great figures. Whatever they state are historical truths.

Why historical truth? Providing a semblance of an indication about the impending future, a definitive word is articulated in some part of it. There are children capable of comprehending the timeframe specified for the rest to materialize. They will understand it and execute it through themselves. They themselves might have stated it. There are certain brief lines in the *Bhagavata*. These should be read. Certain sections must be read with deep attention. If one says that the sage's advice is good; that it is Vedanta; it implies that several good things have been articulated in it. What needs to be conveyed is about the concepts that thinkers have comprehended through reflection and practically applied. Otherwise, thought and action will bifurcate into two distinct entities—which is never beneficial.
Guruvani
